newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis back Labour's Barak over Netanyahu-poll.
newsitem.headline: Israelis back Labour's Barak over Netanyahu-poll.

text.p: Ehud Barak, newly elected leader of the opposition Labour party, bested Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on all counts in a poll published on Friday.

The Gallup poll of 496 Israeli Jews in Maariv daily found if elections were held now 43 percent would vote for former army chief Barak, 35 percent would choose Netanyahu, and 14 percent would not vote for either. Eight percent did not respond.
A Gallup poll for Maariv last Friday, before Barak clinched the Labour party leadership, found 45 percent would vote for Barak and 40 percent for Netanyahu. Fifteen percent did not respond.

Asked which man they thought was better able to deal with security matters, 49 percent said Barak, who years ago was Netanyahu's commander in an elite commando unit, 29 percent chose Netanyahu, and 22 percent did not respond.

There was also a considerable gap on the issue of which politician people believed would be the better peace negotiator: 46 percent chose Barak, 31 percent said Netanyahu and 23 percent did not answer.
The poll had a margin of error of 4.5 percent.

Barak, who backs trading occupied land for peace, vowed on Wednesday after triumphing in Labour's primary to push for early elections to oust the Likud party's Netanyahu, who defeated Barak's predecessor Shimon Peres in elections a year ago.
Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace but has said he will uphold deals signed by the previous Labour-led government.
Israel's next general election is set for 2000.
Netanyahu's coalition, battered in its first year in power by crises in Middle East peacemaking and a corruption scandal, now has a slim majority in parliament, holding 66 of 120 seats.
